name: 野猪林
Boar Wood
before: 林中一片老栗树林，岩公早年怕砖被抢，偷偷把两块半砖埋在一棵老栗树底下，拿石头做了记号。今年栗子结得少，一群野猪饿得发了狂，把林子拱得像翻过的地，记号石也被拱翻了。领头的公猪獠牙有一尺长，正拿鼻子拱着一根露出土的竹签。

This is a stand of old chestnut trees. Years ago, afraid of thieves, Yan Gong secretly buried two half bricks under one of them and marked the spot with a stone. The chestnut crop is thin this year, and a herd of wild boar, mad with hunger, has rooted up the wood like a ploughed field and turned the marker stone over. The lead boar, tusks a foot long, is nosing at a bamboo tag sticking out of the earth.
after: 野猪被赶进深林，你们刨开拱乱的土，两块半砖还在，竹签上的名字被泥糊了，擦干净还认得出。阿梅抱着砖直乐，说太公埋砖的时候就糊涂了，把地方画在了自己的烟袋上，「烟袋上画的是棵松树」。

The boar driven into the deep woods, you dig through the churned soil and find both halves, their tags caked in mud but readable once wiped. A Mei hugs them, laughing: Great-grandpa was muddled even when he buried them, she says, and drew the spot on his tobacco pouch. 'And what he drew was a pine.'

name: 枕砖寨
Brick-Pillow Hold
before: 林中一座山匪的小寨，寨主是个大胖子，睡觉非得枕着一块半砖，说枕着它夜夜梦见自己在赶路，走得浑身舒坦，醒来比没睡还精神。手下的喽啰也想枕，排着队一人枕一夜，为了谁先谁后，天天在寨里打架。

A little bandit hold in the forest is run by an enormous fat chief who can't sleep without a half brick for a pillow. With it under his head, he says, he dreams every night that he's on the road, walking till his whole body feels wonderful, and wakes fresher than if he'd never slept. His men want a turn too, one night each, and they brawl daily over whose turn is next.
after: 山匪被打散，胖寨主抱着砖不撒手，被你们连人带砖抬了出来。他说他梦里的路一直往南，过一条江，上一面崖，崖上钉着木板：「走到崖上，梦就醒了，一回也没走过去。」砖还给了岩公，胖寨主哭丧着脸说，往后只能枕石头了。

The bandits scattered, the fat chief clutches his brick and won't let go, so you carry him out brick and all. The road in his dreams always runs south, he says, across a river and up a cliff with planks pinned to its face. 'When I get onto the cliff, I wake up. Never once got across.' The brick goes back to Yan Gong, and the fat chief, long-faced, says he'll have to sleep on a stone from now on.

name: 挑信营
The Letter-Pole Camp
before: 林中大路上扎着蛊王的一座大营，蛊骑来回巡着，营门口插着一根竹竿，竿上挑着一封信，信封上画着一只金蚕。营里放出话来：这封信是给拿着「另外半块」的人的，谁来取，先过了这一营再说。

A big camp of the Gu King's sits across the forest road, Gu riders patrolling back and forth. At its gate a bamboo pole holds up a letter with a golden silkworm drawn on the envelope. Word has gone out from the camp: the letter is for whoever holds 'the other half', and whoever comes for it must get through the camp first.
after: 大营被打散，你们取下了那封信。信里只有几行字，笔迹很瘦：「三百根丝，一根是空的。金蚕饿，就饿在这一根上。把那块空签的砖送来，我替它找个人拴上，七寨从此太平。」落款是一只金蚕。岩公看了，把信扔进火塘：「他想拿活人去填那一根。」

The camp broken, you take down the letter. It has only a few lines, in a thin, bony hand: 'Three hundred threads, and one is empty. The silkworm's hunger is all in that one. Bring me the brick with the blank tag and I will find someone to tie to it, and the seven villages will have peace.' It is signed with a golden silkworm. Yan Gong reads it and tosses it into the hearth. 'He means to fill that thread with a living man.'

name: 宋家火塘
Song Ge's Hearth
before: 林中一座老吊脚楼，火塘边坐着个瞎眼的老婆婆，是十年前副镖头宋戈的火塘亲。她天天往火塘里添一根柴，说是宋戈走时托过她。几个蛊王派来的寨丁守在楼下，不许外人上去，说婆婆知道「那一根丝」的事，蛊王要她闭嘴。

By the hearth of an old stilt house in the forest sits a blind old woman, who was deputy chief Song Ge's hearth mother ten years ago. Every day she adds one stick to the fire; Song Ge asked her to, she says, when he left. Guards sent by the Gu King hold the stairs and let no outsider up: the old woman knows about 'that one thread', and the King wants her silent.
after: 寨丁被赶走，婆婆摸着你们的手说话。宋戈交砖那一夜跟她讲过：最后那根签不写名字，是因为那个人在雾里走丢了，「名字一写，金蚕就会顺着名字去找他；不写，就等他自己找来」。婆婆添了一根柴：「他说那个人迟早会来。来不了，也会有人替他来。」

The guards chased off, the old woman holds your hands as she talks. The night Song Ge handed over the bricks, he told her why the last tag had no name: that man was lost in the fog. 'Write his name, and the silkworm will follow the name to find him. Leave it blank, and we wait for him to find his own way here.' She adds a stick to the fire. 'He said that man would come sooner or later. And if he couldn't, someone would come in his place.'

name: 砣子碉
Weight-Cheat Tower
before: 林中一座碉楼，碉主是个收山货的小寨主，秤砣不够用，竟拿两块半砖拴在秤杆上当砣，收菌子、收笋干，一斤只给八两的钱。山民们背着山货来卖，被他的家丁挡在碉楼下，谁嫌秤不准，就被打出去。

In a stone watchtower in the forest lives a petty headman who buys mountain produce. Short of scale weights, he has tied two half bricks to his steelyard instead, and for mushrooms and dried bamboo shoots he pays the price of eight ounces for every pound. Hill folk who carry their goods here are held at the foot of the tower by his men, and anyone who complains about the scale is thrown out.
after: 家丁被打散，两块半砖从秤杆上解了下来。碉主还嘴硬，说茶砖比铁砣「压秤」。你们拿真秤一比，一块砖一斤少说亏人二两。山民们冲进碉楼，把这几年少给的钱一笔笔算了回来，碉主的账本被翻得哗哗响。

The men scattered, the two halves come off the steelyard. The headman still insists that tea bricks 'weigh truer' than iron. You check against an honest scale: each brick cheats at least two ounces in the pound. The hill folk storm the tower and reckon up every coin they were shorted over the years, and the pages of the headman's ledger fly.

name: 停蹄坡
Hoof-Stop Slope
before: 林中山坡上，一队蛊骑驮着几只口袋往蛊王寨跑，袋口露出半块茶砖的角。他们的马喂过蛊草，不怕刀也不怕火，冲起来像一堵墙，你们的前排被撞开了两回。慌乱中，有人想起怀里那只吹不响的骨哨，掏出来，使劲吹了一口。

On a forest slope a troop of Gu riders is galloping toward the Gu King's village with sacks slung across their saddles, the corner of a half brick poking from one. Their horses are fed on gu grass and fear neither blade nor fire; they charge like a wall, and twice your front rank is knocked apart. In the confusion someone remembers the bone whistle that makes no sound, pulls it out and blows with all his might.
after: 骨哨还是没有声音，可坡上的马一齐站住了，竖着耳朵，任凭蛊骑怎么抽也不肯再迈一步，蛊骑被你们一个个从马上拽了下来。原来那是马倌唤马的哨，声音尖得人听不见，马听得见。袋里是四块半砖，竹签都在。

The whistle still makes no sound, but every horse on the slope stops dead, ears pricked, and however the riders lash them, they won't take another step. You haul the riders out of their saddles one by one. It was the groom's whistle for calling horses, pitched too high for human ears and not for theirs. In the sacks are four half bricks, tags and all.

name: 布娃楼
The Rag-Doll Loft
before: 死路尽头一座小吊脚楼，楼上住着个七八岁的小姑娘，天天抱着一个布包，像抱娃娃一样，夜里还给它唱歌。布包里是一块半砖，是她在河边捡的。几个吹箭手找上门来，要抢她的「布娃娃」，小姑娘把布包塞进衣服里，缩在楼角，一声不吭。

At the end of a dead end stands a little stilt house, and upstairs lives a girl of seven or eight who carries a cloth bundle everywhere like a doll and sings it to sleep at night. Inside the bundle is a half brick she found by the river. Blowgunners have come to take her 'dolly'. She stuffs the bundle inside her clothes and huddles in a corner without a sound.
after: 吹箭手被打跑了。小姑娘听说这块砖是有主的，一边哭一边把布包解开，说她每天晚上给它唱歌，「怕那个叔叔一个人在路上害怕」。竹签上写着「宋戈」。岩公接过砖，跟小姑娘说好了：以后每天，她还来给它唱一支。

The blowgunners chased off, the girl hears that the brick has an owner. Crying, she unwraps it. She sang to it every night, she says, 'so the uncle wouldn't be scared alone on the road'. The tag reads 'Song Ge'. Yan Gong takes the brick and makes her a promise: every day from now on, she can still come and sing it a song.

name: 免死林
Pardon-Seekers' Wood
before: 林中一伙土司家的逃兵，十几个人，扛着一袋半砖往蛊王寨的方向赶。他们开了小差，土司悬了赏，只有蛊王的地盘土司不敢去，就想拿砖跟蛊王换一张「免死帖」。吊脚楼酒家的老板娘追在后头骂：「那是我买回来的砖！」

A dozen or so deserters from a chieftain's army are hurrying through the forest toward the Gu King's village with a sack of half bricks. There's a bounty on their heads, and the King's land is the one place the chieftain won't follow, so they mean to trade the bricks for a pardon from the Gu King. The landlady of the stilt-house tavern chases after them, cursing: 'Those are my bricks! I bought them back!'
after: 逃兵被打散，袋里的砖抢了回来，是三块。酒家老板娘喘着气说，这三块是她一块一块从贼手里买回来的，藏在酒窖里，昨夜被这伙人偷了。还有两块她没买着，被一个叫老麻的蛊骑带走了。她顿了一下：「老麻是我男人。」

The deserters scattered, you recover the sack: three bricks. Panting, the landlady says she bought these back from thieves one at a time and hid them in her wine cellar, and this lot stole them last night. Two more she never managed to buy; a Gu rider called Old Ma took them. She pauses. 'Old Ma is my husband.'

name: 麻嫂酒家
Ma's Tavern
before: 林中一座吊脚楼酒家，楼下酒坛码得比人还高，往日赶夜路的都在这里歇脚。如今楼被蛊王的一队寨丁征了，当作往蛊王寨运东西的歇站，酒白喝不给钱，老板娘麻嫂只能缩在灶房里。她男人老麻原是蛊骑，半个月前带着两块半砖不见了，寨丁们天天逼她说人在哪儿。

A stilt-house tavern stands in the forest, wine jars stacked taller than a man downstairs, where night travellers used to rest. Now a squad of the Gu King's guards has commandeered it as a way station for hauling goods to his village, drinking free, and the landlady, Sister Ma, has to hide in the kitchen. Her husband, Old Ma, was a Gu rider until half a month ago, when he vanished with two half bricks, and the guards press her daily to say where he is.
after: 寨丁被撵走，酒家重新开张，麻嫂拿米酒跟你们换货，打得满满的。她说老麻不是贼：他当了十年蛊骑，夜夜听金蚕在洞里叫，叫得他睡不着，半个月前揣了两块砖，说要「替那两个人藏起来，不叫蛊王喂了」。他骑着花马往东边的崖下去了。

The guards thrown out, the tavern reopens, and Sister Ma trades you rice wine, measured to the brim. Old Ma's no thief, she says. Ten years a Gu rider, every night hearing the silkworm crying in its cave until he couldn't sleep, and half a month ago he took two bricks, saying he'd 'hide them for those two men so the King can't feed them'. He rode off east on his piebald toward the cliffs.

name: 缺钉沟
Missing-Nail Gully
before: 林中一道山沟，泥里一串马蹄印往东去，是老麻那匹花马的，左前掌缺了一颗钉，印子一看就认得。一伙蛊骑也顺着蹄印在追，领头的扬言：「抓住老麻，砖归蛊王，人归罐子。」你们和蛊骑在沟口撞了个正着。

In a forest gully a line of hoofprints leads east through the mud: Old Ma's piebald, its near fore shoe missing a nail, the print unmistakable. A troop of Gu riders is tracking the same prints, their leader swearing, 'Catch Old Ma, the bricks go to the King and the man goes in a jar.' You and the riders meet head-on at the mouth of the gully.
after: 蛊骑被打退，你们顺着蹄印走到沟底，花马拴在一棵树上，饿得直啃树皮，人不在。马鞍上系着一条麻嫂织的腰带，腰带里塞着一张纸，画着一个洞口，洞口前画了三道弯。

The riders beaten back, you follow the prints to the bottom of the gully. The piebald is tied to a tree, so hungry it's gnawing the bark, and its rider is gone. Round the saddle is a sash woven by Sister Ma, and tucked inside it a scrap of paper showing a cave mouth with three bends drawn in front of it.

name: 三弯洞
Three-Bend Cave
before: 林中崖脚下，三道弯的小路尽头有个洞口，被一伙吹箭手围着。他们正往洞里扔点着的干辣椒捆，想把里头的人熏出来。洞里一阵阵咳嗽，还有个哑着嗓子的声音在骂：「熏死我，砖也不给！」

Under a forest cliff, at the end of a path with three bends, a cave mouth is surrounded by blowgunners. They're tossing burning bundles of dried chillies inside to smoke out whoever is there. From the cave comes coughing, fit after fit, and a hoarse voice swearing: 'Smoke me to death, you still won't get the bricks!'
after: 吹箭手被打跑，洞口的辣椒烟散了。老麻从洞里爬出来，咳得满脸是泪，怀里还紧紧抱着两块半砖。他说这洞往里还有一截，里头有更要紧的东西，他得带你们进去看。

The blowgunners chased off, the chilli smoke clears from the mouth. Old Ma crawls out, coughing till tears stream down his face, two half bricks still hugged tight to his chest. The cave goes further in, he says, and there's something more important inside. He has to show you.

name: 隔壁石缝
The Crack in the Wall
before: 洞的深处离蛊王寨只隔一道石壁，石壁上有条缝，凑近了能听见那边的声音：一种很细很细的叫声，像蚕在啃桑叶，又像有人在很远的地方喊名字。老麻说他就是在这里听了十年。一队蛊王的亲兵从石缝那头摸了过来，要拿泥浆把这条缝堵死。

Deep in the cave only a wall of rock separates you from the Gu King's village, and there's a crack in it. Put your ear to it and you hear the other side: a faint, faint crying, like a silkworm gnawing a mulberry leaf, or someone very far away calling names. This is where Old Ma has listened for ten years. A squad of the King's bodyguards is creeping in from the other side to seal the crack with mud.
after:
亲兵被打退，石缝保住了。老麻把两块砖交给你们，说他没想偷，是想替这两个人藏着：「金蚕要吃，先吃我。」竹签上有一个名字他认得，是那年冬天跟他学骑马的汉人小伙。从石缝里望过去，那边是一个大洞，洞顶垂下千百根金丝，丝都收在一个人身上：一个瘦得只剩一把骨头的老人。「那就是蛊王，」老麻低声说。

消息传回寨老会，岩公捎来一句话：架子满了，二百九十九格，加上你们那一块。

The bodyguards beaten back, the crack stays open. Old Ma hands you the two bricks. He never meant to steal them, he says, only to hide them for their two men. 'If the silkworm wants to eat, let it eat me first.' One name on the tags he knows: a Han lad he taught to ride that winter. Through the crack you see a great cavern, a thousand gold threads hanging from its roof, and every one of them gathered into a single man: an old man wasted to a bundle of bones. 'That's the Gu King,' Old Ma whispers.  Word goes back to the Elders' Council, and Yan Gong sends a message: the rack is full. Two hundred and ninety-nine, and your one besides.

name: 水碓房
The Water-Hammer Mill
before: 林中溪边一排水碓，溪水推着木轮，木轮带着碓杵一下一下地舂米，咚、咚，几个寨子的米都在这里舂。一伙戴黑头巾的山匪占了碓房，在门口立了块牌子：「舂一臼，交一升」，舂好的米一半归他们。不交的，就把谷子倒进溪里。

A row of water hammers stands by a forest stream: the current turns the wheels, the wheels lift the pestles, and they fall into the mortars, thud, thud, husking the rice of several villages. Bandits in black headscarves have taken the mill and put up a sign at the door: 'One quart for every mortar', which comes to half of all the rice. Anyone who won't pay has his grain tipped into the stream.
after: 山匪被撵走，碓杵又咚咚地响起来。舂米的阿公说，近来有一伙「封念人」挨寨上门，说谁家想人想得睡不着，就把那份想念封进罐子里，从此吃得下睡得着。「我老伴去封了，」阿公说，「如今她倒是天天笑，可再也不问我饿不饿了。」

The bandits chased away, the pestles thud again. The old man who husks the rice says a band of 'sealers' has been going door to door: anyone who misses someone so much they can't sleep can have that longing sealed up in a jar, and eat and sleep well ever after. 'My old woman went and had hers sealed,' he says. 'She smiles all day now. But she never asks me any more if I'm hungry.'
first: 抄出山匪的存货：白米二十袋、一串腊肠、两把柴刀，还有舂米剩下的一大堆谷糠，堆得像座小山。阿公说谷糠喂猪都喂不完，你们要用尽管背走。

From the bandits' stores: twenty sacks of white rice, a string of sausages, two wood-cutting knives, and a great heap of rice chaff left from the husking, piled like a little hill. More chaff than the pigs can ever eat, says the old man; if you've any use for it, carry off all you like.
pass: 每次路过，碓房的阿公都给你们舂一袋新米，舂得又白又细：「水推的碓，不要钱。」
Every time you pass, the old man at the mill husks you a fresh sack of rice, white and fine. 'The water works the hammers. Costs nothing.'

name: 封念路
The Sealers' Road
before: 林中路上，一伙封念人赶着骡子挨寨上门，骡背上驮着一摞摞空陶罐和一捆红布。他们正劝一个寡妇封念：「想他做什么？封了就不疼了。」一个十三四岁的姑娘冲过来，拿石子砸他们的骡子，砸得骡子乱跳，罐子摔碎了好几只。封念人身边的寨丁抡起棍子就追她。

On a forest road a party of sealers is leading mules door to door, the beasts loaded with stacks of empty clay jars and a bale of red cloth. They're coaxing a widow: 'Why go on missing him? Seal it up and it won't hurt any more.' A girl of thirteen or fourteen charges up and pelts their mules with stones until the mules buck and several jars smash. The guards with the sealers swing their clubs and go after her.
after: 寨丁被打跑，封念人也跑了。姑娘叫阿扎，她阿公三年前封了念，封的是想一个汉人伙夫的心：那年冬天伙夫小葱住在他家火塘边，教他擀面条。「阿公封了以后天天笑，」阿扎说，「可他连我的名字都懒得喊了。我要把他的罐子找回来。」

The guards chased off, the sealers flee too. The girl is A Zha. Three years ago her grandpa had his longing sealed, his missing of a Han caravan cook: that winter the cook, Xiao Cong, lodged by his hearth and taught him to roll noodles. 'Since it was sealed Grandpa smiles all day,' A Zha says, 'but he can't even be bothered to call my name. I'm going to find his jar and bring it back.'

name: 笑面寨
Smiling Hamlet
before: 林中一座寨子，家家户户都在笑：老人坐在门槛上笑，妇人舂着米笑，见了生人也笑，问什么都答「好，都好」。这寨子封念封得最早，差不多家家封过。阿扎的阿公也坐在寨口，笑眯眯的。几个守寨的蛊骑拦住你们：「这里的人过得好好的，你们别来搅。」

In a forest hamlet every household is smiling. Old folk smile on their doorsteps, women smile as they pound rice, they smile at strangers, and whatever you ask, the answer is 'Fine, all fine.' This hamlet was the first to have its longing sealed, almost every house. A Zha's grandpa sits at the hamlet gate, beaming. Gu riders guarding the place block your way. 'These people are doing perfectly well. Don't come stirring them up.'
after: 蛊骑被赶走。阿公认得阿扎，笑着叫她「娃娃」，却叫不出名字。他灶上挂着一根擀面杖，磨得油光发亮，你们问是谁的，他笑着说想不起来了，「好像是哪个客人落下的，好，都好」。阿扎背过身去，把擀面杖揣进了怀里。

The riders driven off. Grandpa knows A Zha and smiles and calls her 'child', but can't come up with her name. A rolling pin hangs by his stove, worn glossy, and when you ask whose it is he smiles and says he can't remember. 'Some guest left it, I think. Fine, all fine.' A Zha turns her back and tucks the rolling pin inside her coat.

name: 银针铺
The Silver-Pin Smithy
before: 林中一间银匠铺，炉子冷着，风箱蒙了灰。银匠老吴本来打银冠、银项圈，如今蛊王的人把他的银子全收了，逼他只打一样东西：封罐子用的银针，一只罐一根针，针头刻着那户人家的记号。他打得满手血泡，门口还站着两个蛊骑监工。

In a silversmith's shop in the forest the forge is cold and the bellows furred with dust. Old Wu used to make silver crowns and collars, but the Gu King's men have taken all his silver and make him produce one thing only: silver pins to seal the jars, one pin per jar, its head engraved with the household's mark. His hands are covered in blisters, and two Gu riders stand at the door as overseers.
after: 监工被赶走，炉子重新烧了起来。老吴拿银器跟你们换货，说什么也要多送一对银铃。他说银能试毒，封罐用银针，是因为念头封进去会让银发黑，看得出封牢没有。阿扎问他认不认得出阿公的罐子，老吴翻出记号簿：「他家的记号，是一根擀面杖。」

The overseers chased off, the forge roars again. Old Wu trades silverwork for your goods and insists on throwing in a pair of silver bells. Silver tests for poison, he says; the jars are sealed with silver pins because a sealed longing turns the silver black, and that shows whether the seal holds. A Zha asks if he could recognise her grandpa's jar. Old Wu leafs through his book of marks. 'His household's mark is a rolling pin.'

name: 驮罐道
Jar-Mule Trail
before: 林中小道上，一支骡队驮着几十只红布封口的陶罐往东走，罐子用稻草垫着，一路轻轻相碰。护送的是蛊王从山外雇来的镖客，个个带刀，见人就喝退，谁敢多看一眼罐子，先挨一刀背。阿扎远远跟在骡队后头，挨个看罐口的银针。

A mule train carries dozens of red-sealed jars east along a forest path, packed in straw, knocking gently together as they go. Escorting it are caravan guards the Gu King hired from beyond the hills, every one with a blade, who shout off anyone who comes near; look at the jars too long and you get the flat of a sword. A Zha trails the train at a distance, checking the silver pin on every jar.
after: 镖客被打散，骡子停在路边。阿扎一根根针看过去，没有擀面杖的记号。赶骡的老汉说，这些罐都是送去罐林的，「罐林里挂了十年，少说几千只了」；挂满了的旧罐，就从林子尽头的落水洞丢下去。

The escort scattered, the mules stand by the path. A Zha goes over every pin: no rolling pin. The old muleteer says all these jars are bound for the Jar Forest. 'Ten years they've been hanging them there, thousands at the least.' And the old jars, once full, get thrown down the sinkhole at the far end of the forest.

name: 讨念门
The Asking-Back Gate
before: 林中一座小寨门口，一个妇人跪在封念人面前，求他们把封进去的念还给她：三年前她儿子没了，她想得受不了，就封了念；如今她不疼了，可连儿子长什么样都想不起来。「我宁愿疼。」封念人冷笑，说罐子早送走了，叫寨丁把她拖开。

At the gate of a little hamlet a woman kneels before the sealers, begging them to give back what they sealed away. Three years ago she lost her son and missed him past bearing, so she had it sealed. Now it doesn't hurt, but she can't remember what her son looked like. 'I'd rather it hurt.' The sealers sneer that the jar went off long ago and tell the guards to drag her away.
after: 封念人被赶跑了。妇人坐在寨门口，半天没说话。封念人丢下的簿子上记得清楚：她的罐子在罐林东头第七排。阿扎蹲下来握着她的手：「我也在找，找到了一起开。」妇人这才哭出声来，像是很久很久没哭过了。

The sealers driven off, the woman sits at the gate a long while without a word. The register the sealers dropped is clear: her jar hangs in the seventh row at the east end of the Jar Forest. A Zha crouches and takes her hand. 'I'm looking too. When we find them, we'll open them together.' Only then does the woman weep aloud, like someone who hasn't wept in a very long time.

name: 金丝营
Gold-Thread Camp
before: 罐林外扎着一座蛊骑大营，营里的人手腕上都缠着金丝，是蛊王的亲信，丝拴着他们自己的心，听蛊王使唤。营里每天傍晚点一次卯，点完卯，几十个蛊骑骑马进罐林巡一圈，谁也不许在林里停步。

Outside the Jar Forest stands a big camp of Gu riders, every one with gold thread round his wrist: the Gu King's trusted men, their own hearts tied to do his bidding. Each evening the camp calls the roll, and then dozens of riders ride a circuit through the Jar Forest, where no one is allowed to stop.
after: 大营被你们打散。一个手腕缠丝的俘虏说了实话：「金蚕吃的是心。千里号那些人的心拴在丝那头，太远了，吃不着；吃不着他们，就只好吃想他们的心。」想得越苦越顶饿，所以封念人专挑等人等得最久的人家。

You scatter the camp. A prisoner with thread on his wrist tells the truth. 'The silkworm eats hearts. The Qianli men's hearts are tied at the far end of the threads, too far away to reach. If it can't eat them, it eats the hearts that miss them.' The bitterer the longing, the more it fills, and that's why the sealers pick the households that have waited longest.

name: 酸汤灶
Sour-Soup Kitchens
before: 林中一处五岔路口，几口大灶熬着酸汤，是来往罐林那条路上歇脚吃饭的地方，一碗酸汤泡饭，够走一天山路。一伙刀客占了灶，汤照熬，却只卖给蛊骑，过路的山民一碗也买不着，还被他们拿汤勺敲着脑门赶走。

At a five-way fork in the forest, big stoves simmer sour soup; travellers on the Jar Forest road stop here to eat, and one bowl of rice in sour soup keeps you walking a whole day. A band of swordsmen has taken the stoves. The soup still simmers, but they sell it only to Gu riders, and hill folk passing by can't buy a bowl; they're driven off with a ladle rapped on the forehead.
after: 刀客被赶走，灶里的火又旺了，山民端着碗排起了队。熬汤的大婶说，罐林里夜里常有人哭，是封了念的人自己走进林子，站在自家的罐子底下，什么也想不起来，就是哭，「哭完了，又笑着回家」。

The swordsmen chased off, the stoves blaze again and hill folk queue with their bowls. The woman who brews the soup says people can often be heard crying in the Jar Forest at night: sealed folk who walk into the woods by themselves and stand under their own jars. They can't remember anything. They just cry. 'And when they're done crying, they go home smiling.'
first: 抄出刀客囤的糟辣椒六坛、腌笋两筐、一缸米酸、二十只风干的山鸡，还有一口铜锅，大婶说是她家祖传的，追着要了回去。

From the swordsmen's hoard: six jars of fermented chilli, two baskets of pickled bamboo shoots, a vat of rice-sour starter, twenty air-dried pheasants, and a copper pot, which the soup woman says is a family heirloom and chases you to get back.
pass: 每次路过，大婶都给你们盛满满一碗酸汤泡饭，多放一勺糟辣椒：「辣一下，心就醒了。」
Every time you pass, the soup woman fills you a brimming bowl of rice in sour soup with an extra spoon of fermented chilli. 'A good burn wakes the heart.'

name: 红罐窑
The Red-Jar Kiln
before: 死路尽头一座龙窑，顺着山坡爬了十几丈，窑火日夜不熄，烧的全是封念用的陶罐。窑工们被铁链拴着干活，守窑的是蛊王最精的吹箭手和蛊骑。窑口堆着小山似的新罐，红布已经裁好，一捆一捆码在旁边。

At the end of a dead end a dragon kiln crawls a hundred feet up the hillside, its fire never out day or night, firing nothing but jars for sealing. The potters work in iron chains, guarded by the Gu King's best blowgunners and riders. New jars are heaped like a hill at the kiln mouth, and the red cloth, already cut, is stacked beside them bale by bale.
after: 精兵被打退，窑工的铁链砸开了，窑火也熄了。老窑工翻开窑口的记数板，一道一道的刻痕，十年烧了三千多只罐。「烧一只，寨里就少一个会想人的人，」他说，「我烧了十年，自己的念也封了，今天才觉得手疼。」

The elite beaten back, the potters' chains are struck off and the kiln fire dies. The old master potter turns over the tally board at the kiln mouth, notch after notch: more than three thousand jars in ten years. 'Every jar I fire, the villages lose one more person who can miss someone,' he says. 'Ten years I fired them, and had my own longing sealed too. Only today do my hands hurt.'

name: 忘乡人
The Man Who Forgot Home
before: 林中一座小寨里有个北方口音的汉子，在寨里放了七年狗，乐呵呵的，谁也想不起他是从哪儿来的。他自己也想不起来：七年前他想家想得要寻死，封了念，从此再不提家。今天一伙吹箭手来抓他，说蛊王要他去罐林看罐：「这人没念头，最听话。」

In a little forest hamlet lives a man with a northern accent who has herded the village dogs for seven years, cheerful as anything, and nobody remembers where he came from. Neither does he. Seven years ago he was so homesick he wanted to die, had it sealed, and never mentioned home again. Today blowgunners have come for him: the Gu King wants him to watch over the jars. 'A man with no longings does as he's told.'
after: 吹箭手被打跑，汉子还笑着给狗喂食。你们问他家在哪儿，他想了半天，只想出一句：「有条大河，冬天冻上。」阿扎说等找到罐子，也帮他找他的那一只。他挠挠头，笑着说好，像在答应别人的事。

The blowgunners chased off, the man goes on feeding the dogs, smiling. You ask where his home is. He thinks a long while and comes up with one line: 'There's a big river. Freezes in winter.' A Zha says that when she finds her jar she'll look for his too. He scratches his head and smiles and says all right, as if agreeing to something for somebody else.

name: 胡蜂岭
Hornet Ridge
before: 林中山岭上一棵老枫树挂着个水缸大的胡蜂窝，过路的人一靠近，蜂群就扑下来。封念人专走这条岭，因为蜂子不蜇他们：他们身上抹着蛊王给的药膏。阿扎要从这里抄近路去罐林，你们刚上岭，蜂群已经嗡嗡地飞了出来。

On a forest ridge an old maple holds a hornets' nest as big as a water vat, and the swarm comes down on anyone who passes. The sealers always take this ridge, because the hornets don't sting them: they're smeared with a salve the Gu King gives them. A Zha wants the shortcut to the Jar Forest, and you've barely set foot on the ridge before the swarm comes humming out.
after: 你们拿湿草点起浓烟，把蜂群熏回了窝，翻过了岭。站在岭上往下看，林子里星星点点全是红的，像一树树结满了熟透的果子，一直红到看不见的地方。阿扎看了很久，说：「那么多。」

You light wet grass, smoke the swarm back into its nest and cross the ridge. From the crest the forest below is spattered with red, as if tree after tree were loaded with ripe fruit, red as far as the eye can reach. A Zha looks for a long time. 'So many.'

name: 听蚕坛
The Listeners' Altar
before: 罐林边的林子里，听蚕会的人搭了一座竹坛，坛上供着一只金纸扎的蚕，信徒们围着竹坛跪了一圈，一边敲竹梆一边念：「蚕饿了，蚕饿了。」他们拦着去罐林的路，说外人进林，会惊了蚕神。

In the woods beside the Jar Forest the Silkworm Listeners have built a bamboo altar with a silkworm of gold paper on it. The faithful kneel in a ring around it, knocking their clappers and chanting, 'The silkworm is hungry, the silkworm is hungry.' They block the road to the Jar Forest: outsiders going in will startle the silkworm god.
after: 信徒们被赶散，纸蚕被风吹进了沟里。会首被捉住后哭丧着脸说，他们并不想害人，只是怕：「蚕要是饿死了，丝就断了，那些拴着丝的人，就再也找不着回来的路了。」阿扎冷冷地说：「那就拿该喂的东西去喂，别拿我阿公喂。」

The faithful scattered, the paper silkworm blows away into a ditch. Their leader, caught, says miserably that they never meant harm; they're afraid. 'If the silkworm starves, the threads break, and everyone tied by them will never find the way back.' A Zha answers coldly: 'Then feed it what it ought to eat. Not my grandpa.'

name: 鬼医寮
The Ghost Doctor's Lodge
before: 死路尽头一座竹寮，住着寨里的鬼医麻先生，治了一辈子病。门口守着他花钱雇来的刀客和吹箭手，寮后的竹笼里关着十几个人，都是过路的外乡人：货郎、背夫、走亲戚的汉人。麻先生每隔几天挑一个，送去给封念人封念。寮门口晒着一排小孩的鞋。

At the end of a dead end stands a bamboo lodge where Doctor Ma, the villages' ghost doctor, has healed the sick all his life. Swordsmen and blowgunners he has paid stand at his door, and in bamboo cages behind the lodge he keeps a dozen or so travellers from outside: peddlers, porters, Han folk visiting kin. Every few days the doctor picks one and hands him to the sealers. A row of children's shoes is set out to dry at his door.
after: 刀客被打散，竹笼砸开了。麻先生不跑，坐在门口说：去年金蚕饿极了，夜里开始喊寨里娃娃的名字，喊走了两个。「我拿外乡人的念喂它，它就不来喊娃娃了。我救下了十一个娃娃。」门口那排鞋，是那十一个娃娃的。没人替他求情，也没人骂得出口。

The swordsmen scattered, the cages are smashed open. Doctor Ma doesn't run. He sits at his door and explains. Last year the silkworm grew so hungry it began calling village children's names at night, and two of them walked away. 'I feed it strangers' longings, and it stops calling the children. I've saved eleven children.' The shoes at his door belong to those eleven. No one pleads for him. No one can quite bring themselves to curse him either.

name: 罐账楼
The Jar Ledger House
before: 林中一座木楼是封念人的账房，楼里一排排账簿记着每一只罐：哪一家、封的什么念、哪一天封的、挂在罐林哪一排。几个账先生带着寨丁守楼，见你们来了，慌着往火盆里扔账簿。

A timber house in the forest is the sealers' counting house, its shelves of ledgers recording every jar: which household, what longing, what day it was sealed, which row of the Jar Forest it hangs in. A few clerks and their guards hold the house, and when they see you coming they start throwing ledgers into the brazier in a panic.
after: 账先生被按住，账簿抢下了大半。阿扎翻到擀面杖记号那一页，脸一下白了：「三年前封，挂西头第二排。去年十月，罐满，丢落水洞。」账先生缩着脖子解释：念封久了，罐就满了，满了挂不下，就丢进落水洞，「水会把它们带到蛊王那儿去」。

The clerks pinned down, most of the ledgers are saved. A Zha finds the page with the rolling-pin mark and goes white. 'Sealed three years ago, hung west end, second row. Last tenth month: jar full, thrown down the sinkhole.' The clerk, hunching, explains: a longing sealed long enough fills its jar, full jars can't all be hung, so they're dropped down the sinkhole. 'The water carries them to the Gu King.'

name: 征夫坪
The Levy Ground
before: 罐林外一片开阔的坪子，蛊王的人在这里征夫：七寨的青壮被拉来扛罐、挂罐，一寨十个人，不来的，就封他家一个人的念抵数。坪上旗子插了一圈，寨丁、吹箭手、蛊骑各占一角，被征来的人排着长队，一个个领罐子。

On an open ground outside the Jar Forest the Gu King's men are raising a levy: able-bodied men of the seven villages dragged in to carry and hang jars, ten from each village, and if one fails to come, someone in his household has their longing sealed to make up the number. Banners ring the ground, guards, blowgunners and riders each holding a corner, while the conscripts queue to be handed their jars one by one.
after: 征夫坪被你们打散，被征来的人扔下罐子跑回了家。领头的寨丁被捉住，说起落水洞：那洞在罐林最西头，洞口往下全是黑的，丢下去的罐从来听不见落地，「底下是水，一直往东流，流到哪儿谁也不知道」。

You break up the levy, and the conscripts drop their jars and run home. The captured guard captain talks about the sinkhole. It's at the far west end of the Jar Forest, black all the way down, and no one ever hears a jar land. 'There's water at the bottom, flowing east. Where it goes, nobody knows.'

name: 罐林
The Jar Forest
before: 罐林到了。千百棵树上挂满了陶罐，罐口封着红布，风一吹，罐子轻轻碰在一起，咚、咚，像很多人在小声敲门。林子里很静，有几个手腕缠丝的人站在树下，仰着头，一动不动。几个守林的蛊骑从树后转了出来。

The Jar Forest. Thousands of trees hung with clay jars sealed in red cloth, and when the wind blows they knock softly together, tock, tock, like many people tapping quietly at a door. It is very still. A few people with thread on their wrists stand beneath the trees, faces upturned, not moving. Gu riders on watch step out from behind the trunks.
after: 守林的蛊骑被赶走。阿扎找到西头第二排，那棵树上空着一个钩子。东头第七排，那个妇人的罐子还在，她踮着脚把罐子抱了下来，没敢开。阿扎说先别开，这是银匠老吴叮嘱的：「金蚕没喂饱以前，开了罐，它闻着味儿，又要来抢。」

The riders driven off, A Zha finds the second row at the west end: on that tree, one empty hook. In the seventh row at the east end the woman's jar is still there. She stands on tiptoe, lifts it down, and doesn't dare open it. Not yet, A Zha tells her; Old Wu the silversmith warned them. 'Open a jar before the silkworm's been fed, and it'll smell it and come to snatch it back.'

name: 挂罐歌
The Jar-Hanger's Song
before: 罐林深处住着个挂罐的老汉，十年来林里的罐子都是他挂的。他每挂一只，就编一句歌记下位置，哪家的罐在哪棵树哪根枝，全在他的歌里。蛊骑听说了，要拉他去封念，叫他把那支歌也忘掉。老汉抱着树干不撒手，嘴里还在唱。

Deep in the Jar Forest lives the old man who has hung every jar in it for ten years. For each jar he hangs he makes up a line of song to remember its place, which household's jar is on which branch of which tree, all of it in his song. The Gu riders have heard, and mean to drag him off to be sealed so he'll forget the song too. The old man hugs a tree trunk and won't let go, still singing.
after: 蛊骑被打跑，老汉喘着气把歌唱给阿扎听，唱到西头第二排，停了：「那一只，去年十月丢进了落水洞。」他说他也想知道丢下去的罐子去了哪儿，「水往东流，可东边哪儿冒出来，我活了七十年也不知道」。阿扎想起了碓房里那一大堆谷糠。

The riders chased off, the old man, still panting, sings for A Zha. At the second row of the west end he stops. 'That one went down the sinkhole last tenth month.' He'd like to know where the dropped jars go himself. 'The water runs east, but where it comes up in the east, seventy years I've lived and never found out.' A Zha thinks of the great heap of chaff at the water mill.

name: 落水洞
The Sinkhole
before: 罐林最西头，一条溪水流到这里，一头扎进山脚的一个黑洞，不见了，这就是落水洞。洞口拦着竹栅，几个寨丁守着，正把一筐满了的旧罐往洞里倒，罐子落进黑暗里，一点声音也没有。

At the far west end of the Jar Forest a stream runs up to the foot of the hill and plunges into a black hole and is gone: the sinkhole. A bamboo grille fences the mouth, and the guards posted there are tipping a basket of old, full jars into it. They fall into the dark without a sound.
after: 寨丁被打跑，你们扒着洞口往下看，只听见底下哗哗的水声。阿扎把从碓房背来的一大袋谷糠倒进溪里，谷糠打着旋，跟着溪水钻进了洞。「水从哪儿冒出来，糠就从哪儿冒出来，」她说，「我们去下游等。」

The guards chased off, you lean over the mouth and hear only water rushing far below. A Zha empties a big sack of chaff from the water mill into the stream, and it swirls and vanishes into the hole with the water. 'Wherever the water comes up, the chaff comes up with it,' she says. 'We go downstream and wait.'

name: 黑巾寨
Black-Scarf Stockade
before: 野地里一座大寨，是黑头巾山匪的老窝，几百号人，碓房那伙就是从这里派出去的。寨子横在往东南去的路上，过路的要交「头巾钱」，交了钱领一条黑头巾戴上，才算「自己人」。阿扎急着去下游等谷糠，一头撞上了他们的寨门。

A big stockade in the open is the lair of the black-scarf bandits, several hundred strong; the gang at the water mill was sent out from here. It sits square across the road south-east, and travellers pay 'scarf money' and are given a black headscarf to wear, which makes them 'one of us'. In her hurry to get downstream for the chaff, A Zha runs straight into their gate.
after: 黑头巾山匪被打散，满地是扔掉的头巾。匪首被捉住，倒说了件有用的事：每到雨季，东南泽地里有一处泉眼会冒出碎陶片和烂红布，「我们还以为是哪个寨子往泉眼里祭神」。阿扎听完，拔腿就往东南跑。

The bandits scattered, the ground is littered with discarded scarves. The captured chief does let slip something useful: every rainy season a spring in the south-eastern marshes coughs up broken pottery and scraps of rotten red cloth. 'We thought some village was making offerings into it.' A Zha hears that and takes off running south-east.
